_whose: This file belongs to the person who runs Granite Record, like bill_notes.json and docket_corrections.json. Claude drafted the rows on 5 October 2026 from a copy of Ballotpedia's list of New Hampshire ballot measures saved that day, for that person's review, and on 7 October 2026 read the Secretary of State's certified count of each question beside it. On 7 October 2026 the person approved the Secretary of State as the source of every row the voters have decided -- its count, its listing of the question and where the count is printed -- with the two No counts where Ballotpedia differs corrected to the Secretary of State's, and Ballotpedia's figures kept on each row as the cross-check. Read them; the file is yours.
_what: The statewide vote on each constitutional amendment both chambers sent to the voters, one row per CACR: the general election it went to, how its source lists the question, and, once the voters have decided it, the Yes and No votes cast on it as the Secretary of State certified them, with where they are printed. The one still to come has no count yet, and names Ballotpedia's list as its source until the count is in. Copied by hand from the source each row names. No generator writes this file, and preflight fails if any build_* or fetch_* script opens it for writing (HANDMADE).
_why: The General Court's docket records the voters' answer for nine of these amendments ('AMENDMENT FAILED REFERENDUM(278,998-178,817)') and for the eight since 2006 records nothing after the second chamber's vote, so those read 'went to the voters' with no answer. The voters' answer is public record, and this is where it comes from.
_how: An amendment needs two thirds of those voting on it (the constitution, Part II, Article 100). The build works the outcome out from yes and no against two thirds and does not read one from here: several of these won a majority and failed. A row with yes and no null is an election still to come, and its source is the list that names the question until the Secretary of State's count is in.

_fields.term: The CACR's term, as everywhere else on the site.
_fields.bill: The CACR's number, as data/bills.json writes it.
_fields.election: The day of the state general election it went to.
_fields.label: How the source lists the question, as written: the Secretary of State's 'Question No. 4' in the 1993 Manual, 'Question 1' in the 1999 one, and so on. In parentheses where the Manual printed that year's one question with no number -- '(the only question; unnumbered)', as the reading of 7 October wrote it -- which is a description and not its words, and the pages say it in their own sentence, without quotation marks. For 2018 the Secretary of State's spreadsheet numbers the questions without naming them, and which number is which CACR rests on Ballotpedia's labels and its matching counts (that row's note). For the election still to come, Ballotpedia's name for it.
_fields.yes: Votes for, as the Secretary of State certified them: the statewide line of its results. A blank ballot is not a vote cast on the question and is in neither count.
_fields.source: The page the figures were read from. From 2016, the Secretary of State's results page for that general election on sos.nh.gov, whose constitutional-question spreadsheet gives the statewide total; sos.nh.gov holds nothing earlier. Before 2016, the page of NHPR's Elections Database scan of the Department of State's Manual for the General Court -- the 'Red Book' the docket's own referendum lines cite -- that prints the count. For the election still to come, Ballotpedia's list of New Hampshire ballot measures, which names the question; the Secretary of State's list of the 2026 questions has not been read.
_fields.cite: Where the figures are printed, as a reader would look them up: 'Manual for the General Court 1993, p. 442 (NHPR's scan)', or '2018 general election results, sos.nh.gov'.
_fields.note: Something about the row a person checking it should know.
_fields.ballotpedia: Ballotpedia's figures for the same question, read on 5 October 2026 from its list of New Hampshire ballot measures, which was this file's source until 7 October: yes and no, label (its Title column), described (its description, abridged only where noted, for checking the match), source and read. Kept as the cross-check on the 17 rows the voters had decided by 7 October 2026; a row decided after that needs none, and is checked against one only where it has one. They equal the Secretary of State's on 15 of the 17 decided rows. On two, Ballotpedia's No differs, and neither changes the outcome: CACR 7 of 1992, 204,457 against the Secretary of State's 204,475, two digits transposed; and CACR 41 of 2006, 100,686 against 100,688.
_fields.described: On the row still to come, its source's description of the measure; on the others it is inside ballotpedia.
_fields.match: Why this measure is this CACR: its title, the election its own text names, and the docket row that sent it (or recorded the referendum).
